newsitem.title: FRANCE: Talks progress but French doctors strike to go on.
newsitem.headline: Talks progress but French doctors strike to go on.

text.p: Striking French junior hospital doctors said on Friday talks had progressed with Social Affairs Minister Jacques Barrot but they would continue a 16-day-old strike over a disputed health cost control plan.
"Now we're listening to each other, but conditions are not yet ripe for us to end the strike," doctors' spokesman Olivier Charrois said.

Barrot and junior health minister Herve Gaymard met a delegation of strikers after hospital doctors from across France staged a show of force in Paris on Thursday, with at least 10,000 people taking part in a protest march.
The doctors, on strike in 22 of the country's 26 teaching hospitals, are demanding the scrapping of automatic fines on doctors in regions which exceed government health spending targets.
But Barrot told Europe 1 radio the measure was essential as a safeguard against overspending until new standard medical procedures take root.
The centre-right government has imposed health spending curbs to bring down the welfare deficit and help France qualify for a single European currency in 1999.
Barrot said the government would probably formally promulgate on Saturday an agreement between the national health insurance fund and two health professionals' trade unions which support the reform.
